differences.what: cornice: the print's brackets are paired, deeper and closer, over a frieze that reads dark from end to end; the build's are single, evenly spaced, over a light band
differences.how: T-2369: K10 lays the brackets in pairs on the piers between the frieze lights, stations 1.6 m apart, and the whole cornice from frieze to crown is painted dark

differences.what: south wall: the print shows a canted bay on the brick side wall behind the front; the build's side is flat
differences.how: T-2369: a K08 canted oriel on the south wall's upper storey, 1.1 m out, sill at the second floor, hood top at about 10.1 m, light stone faces under a deep dark hood, on eight corbel courses, where the print shows it

differences.what: stoop: the print's steps are fewer and narrower between iron hand-rails; the build's are a long stone flight with stone cheeks
differences.how: T-2369: the door is at the stoop's head, 1.7 m (ten risers), the stoop 1.7 m wide with no stone cheeks, between the K11 kit's iron stair rails scrolled at the foot

differences.what: portico: the print's porch stands closer to the wall and reads flatter; the build's projects further, with deep open sides
differences.how: T-2369: a barrel from the wall to 1.4 m out under an elliptical ring springing at 4.8 m, on impost blocks and columns 0.9 m before the wall, the shafts where the print's stand (X 1177 and 1412); the review render is lit from the print's own sun so the portico's shade is compared too

differences.what: fence line: the build's fence stood 6.9 m before the front, well short of the print's posts
differences.how: T-2369: the line is 4.7 m from the front; the lot's south corner post and the gate posts fall where the print's stand

differences.what: colour of the stone, the brick, the iron, the sash, the door and the cornice's paint: the print is monochrome (the door reads black in the portico's shade; the render's shows brown)
the oriel's corbelling: the print shows it only as a dark wedge in shadow under the oriel, so the courses' depth and whether it is stone corbelling or brackets are not seen
the centre bay's two frieze lights and the frieze's own surface: hidden in the print by what may be a vine over the cornice
the fence's foot: the print's reads about 0.5 m above the walk near the stoop; the walk, the yard's grade and a coping cannot be told apart, so the kit's 0.25 m curb is kept
the south wall behind the oriel and the north bay: out of the picture or hidden by the neighbour

three bays, entrance in the middle; round-arched paired upper lights, tall principal windows and paired basement lights, each under a long keystone; banded stone to the frieze; frontispiece and arched portico; iron guards and grilles; fence on iron posts

front walk and gate: the print shows a light paved walk running in from the public walk to the stoop's foot and the gateway there standing open, two people in it; the build had lawn to the stoop and both entrance leaves shut
differences.how: T-3214: a K14 yard, its flagged front walk from the stoop's foot through the entrance gate to the public walk, the gate's leaves drawn open 70 degrees

differences.what: the south passage's floor and the ground outside its gate: the print shows light ground and a shrub before the fence's south end, the build the kit's cinder walk; a monochrome print gives a tone, not a material, and the planting is the front-yard plantings' (T-3203)

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153).
